Hi Aisha — thanks for the RFQ and context. Short answer: we can do a few pragmatic paths depending on how you want billing and crediting to look. Attached is a one-page commercial and a proposed amendment (PDF). High level options below — pick the one that maps to how your finance/procurement wants to operate and we’ll formalize.

1) One-time top-up (pro-rata invoice)
   - Customer purchases additional committed units now; billing pro-rated to Jan 31, 2027.
   - No change to renewal; top-up priced at list with a 7–10% one-time bulk uplift discount for 50k+.

2) Staged annualize (voucher-style credit)
   - We issue credit vouchers that convert to committed units at renewal; immediate capacity and partial discount (10–15%)
   - Useful if you want to smooth cashflow; vouchers applied against invoice at Jan 31 renewal.

3) Bridge credit + co-term amendment (recommended if you want predictable unit economics)
   - We create an amendment to co-term the uplift to Jan 31 and apply a stepped discount based on uplift bucket: 50k→10%, 100k→15%, 250k+→20%.
   - Billing: initial pro-rata invoice for remainder of term, then annualized amount billed at renewal.

A few notes:
- SLA/priority: we can include a temporary surge priority add-on during the uplift window (1–3 months) for an incremental fee; otherwise standard latency SLOs apply.
- Invoice timing: typical workflow is pro-rata charge processed within 30 days of amendment execution; renewal billing on Jan 31 cycle.

Next steps: 30-min call with your procurement this week or early next. If procurement prefers a true-up vs vouchers, we’ll recommend option 3 with credits converted to committed units at renewal.

I attached Redwood-Aspire-Proposal-2026-09-21.pdf with a worked example using the token profile you sent. Let me know a few times and I’ll get Ben/RevOps looped for billing flow.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood-Aspire-Proposal-2026-09-21.pdf (pdf)

Team — forwarding Aspire thread. They asked for: co-term to Jan 31, example math for 75k / 150k uplifts, and they prefer a true-up credits flow (procurement ask). They also want temporary surge priority for ~8 weeks.

Quick proposed internal options (numbers illustrative, see attached model):

Offer A (conservative) — 75k uplift
- Pro-rata charge for remainder of term (Oct 1–Jan 31 = 4 months): 75k * (4/12) = $25,000 initial invoice.
- Stepped discount applies to uplift only: 75k bucket -> 12% discount on uplift units (saves $9k annually when annualized).
- Margin impact: ~18% reduction vs list for uplift (acceptable).

Offer B (aggressive) — 150k uplift
- Pro-rata: 150k * (4/12) = $50,000 initial invoice.
- Discount: 15% on uplift, plus we annualize remainder at renewal for blended rate.
- Include 8-week surge priority add-on at $3,500 flat (covers priority capacity & monitoring).

Ask: Ben — can you approve up to 15% discount on the uplift bucket for this account? Priyom — confirm billing flow if procurement wants a true-up credit (we should issue a credit memo style record and convert at renewal). If legal needs to review the amendment draft, I’ll drop in the doc and route for signature.
